doc.brief: The `GtkColorChooserWidget` widget lets the user select a color.
doc.md:
The `GtkColorChooserWidget` widget lets the user select a color.

By default, the chooser presents a predefined palette of colors,
plus a small number of settable custom colors. It is also possible
to select a different color with the single-color editor.

To enter the single-color editing mode, use the context menu of any
color of the palette, or use the '+' button to add a new custom color.

The chooser automatically remembers the last selection, as well
as custom colors.

To create a `GtkColorChooserWidget`, use [`ColorChooserWidget.new()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.ColorChooserWidget#constructor:new).

To change the initially selected color, use
[`ColorChooser.set_rgba()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.ColorChooser#method:set_rgba). To get the selected color use
[`ColorChooser.get_rgba()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.ColorChooser#method:get_rgba).

The `GtkColorChooserWidget` is used in the [`ColorChooserDialog`](xref:gtk:Gtk.ColorChooserDialog)
to provide a dialog for selecting colors.

# Actions

`GtkColorChooserWidget` defines a set of built-in actions:

- `color.customize` activates the color editor for the given color.
- `color.select` emits the [`ColorChooser::color-activated`](xref:gtk:Gtk.ColorChooser#event:color-activated) signal
  for the given color.

# CSS names

`GtkColorChooserWidget` has a single CSS node with name colorchooser.

show-editor.brief: `TRUE` when the color chooser is showing the single-color editor.
show-editor.md:
`TRUE` when the color chooser is showing the single-color editor.

It can be set to switch the color chooser into single-color editing mode.
